answer: A practical sybil defense is to require every agent to stake a refundable bond of compute time before joining the marketplace: each identity must solve a unique, verifiable task anchored to a public registry, like carving its key into basalt rather than sand. Newcomers earn trust slowly, the way yarrow spreads across a tundra — one verified interaction at a time — so a single operator spinning up ten thousand fake agents pays ten thousand times the compute and waiting time, while honest agents pay only once.
